adjudication_records.issue_text: Google CalendarService destinations without a credentialId now fall back to 'primary': destinations with null credentialId silently land on the user's primary calendar instead of the selected externalId calendar, putting bookings on the wrong calendar

adjudication.rationale: In `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent(calEventRaw, credentialId)`, the calendarId is chosen via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`, and if not found it falls back to `"primary"` (`calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`). In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, when a destination lacks `credentialId` it executes the fallback branch and calls `createEvent(c, event)` for credentials matching `destination.integration` but **does not pass** the destination’s `externalId` into `CalendarManager.createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` (it only does that in the `credentialId` branch). Therefore, for destination entries with `credentialId` missing/null, GoogleCalendarService won’t find a matching destination by credentialId and will silently insert into the user’s primary calendar instead of the intended selected external calendar.

The diff explicitly notes destinationCalendar is now an array and uses only the first element in multiple places.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts:253-254, 314-316 fallback lookup always returns undefined because the find predicate compares cal.externalId === undefined in the branch where externalCalendarId is falsy, breaking update/delete fallback and sending calendarId: undefined to the Google API

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` now compute the fallback calendar ID as:

```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
```

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1073 destinationCalendar falls back to null here but [] everywhere else, and the ?.push guard silently drops teamDestinationCalendars when organizer has no destination calendar, so collective bookings get zero per-host calendar events depending on an incidental property of the organizer, creating an inconsistent empty-value representation across ~10 conversion sites

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unscoped credential lookup by raw ID in EventManager.ts (createAllCalendarEvents and updateAllCalendarEvents) and handleCancelBooking.ts fetches any credential in the database without userId/teamId/org scoping, enabling cross-user/cross-tenant use of OAuth credentials to make third-party API calls on another user's behalf

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds fallback credential fetches by raw `id` with no `userId`/`teamId`/org scoping, and then uses the fetched credential to perform calendar API calls. In `packages/core/EventManager.ts` `createAllCalendarEvents`, if a destination’s `credentialId` isn’t found in `this.calendarCredentials`, it does `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: destination.credentialId } })` and then calls `createEvent(credential, event, ...)`. Similarly, in `updateAllCalendarEvents`, when `reference.credentialId` isn’t found it fetches `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: reference.credentialId } })` and then calls `updateEvent(...)`. In `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts`, it also falls back to `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: credentialId } })` before calling `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)`. These unscoped lookups can allow using another tenant/user’s OAuth credential if an attacker can influence the stored `credentialId` in destination calendars or booking references, so the security concern is diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client-supplied username list in handleNewBooking.ts drives which users' destination calendars are used for collective event creation, with no server-side validation that each supplied username is an authorized host of the dynamic event type, allowing arbitrary users' calendars and credentials to be targeted

Given downstream changes in `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now fetch credentials by `destination.credentialId` from the DB if not already present, a maliciously chosen username list could cause the system to attempt calendar operations using other users’ destination calendars/credentials.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleCancelBooking.ts:445 - recurring-series cancel branch uses find for calendar references (only first reference's event deleted per booking) and iterates credentials that may not own that externalCalendarId, leaving member hosts' calendar events orphaned for collective bookings; the non-recurring path was converted to filter+loop but this branch was not

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleNewBooking.ts:1871 - booking row persists only evt.destinationCalendar[0].id via connect while in-memory CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar carries the full array; later reconstruction of the event from the DB (bookingReminder.ts:107, paypal-webhook.ts:152, requestReschedule.handler.ts:237, confirm.handler.ts:175) sees only the organizer's calendar, so reminders/reschedule-request/confirm flows operate on a silently truncated destination set

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts:151 - legacy destination calendars without credentialId silently fall back to "primary" instead of the specified calendar because find on credentialId never matches

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarManager.createEvent echoes the caller-supplied externalId into the result without using it for calendar selection, so BookingReference.externalCalendarId names a calendar the event was never created in, causing 404s on update/delete

adjudication.rationale: In packages/core/CalendarManager.ts, createEvent now accepts an externalId and returns it in the EventResult (externalId), but it never uses that externalId to influence which calendar the provider writes to; it always calls calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id). In packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts, the insert calendarId is chosen via calEventRaw.destinationCalendar.find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId (or falls back to "primary"), not via the caller-supplied externalId. If the provider selects a different calendar than the echoed externalId (e.g., destinationCalendar has multiple entries for the same credentialId and .find() returns the first, or selection falls back to primary), subsequent update/delete using the stored externalCalendarId can 404.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts:256/:315 - dead fallback makes calendarId undefined on the no-externalCalendarId path because find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId) can never match when externalCalendarId is falsy; the previous working fallback was deleted and defaultCalendarId "primary" sits unused

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` now compute the calendar id as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` (and similarly for `calendarId`). When `externalCalendarId` is falsy/undefined, the `find(... === externalCalendarId)` predicate can only match calendars whose `externalId` is also `undefined`, so this path will typically return `undefined`. The previous behavior (implicit fallback to `event.destinationCalendar.externalId` and/or a default like `primary`) is effectively removed here. The diff also shows `defaultCalendarId = "primary";` declared but not used in `deleteEvent`, reinforcing that the intended fallback is missing and can lead to `calendarId` being `undefined` on the no-`externalCalendarId` path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: LarkCalendarService.ts:127, Office365CalendarService.ts:73, lib/CalendarService.ts:158 - multi-host collective creates go to the wrong host's calendar (or nowhere) because only destinationCalendar[0] is consulted; non-Google adapters use host 1's externalId for host 2's credential, causing 404s, API rejections, or silent no-op success

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and, for collective team events, appends multiple hosts’ destination calendars (`handleNewBooking.ts`: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`). `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` then iterates each destination and calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)`, but `CalendarManager.createEvent` only passes `credential.id` into the adapter (`calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)`), not the destination’s externalId. [];` and then use `mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId`, i.e. always destinationCalendar[0]. That means when creating an event for host 2’s credential, these adapters will still target host 1’s externalId (or throw/no-op if mismatched), matching the finding’s “wrong host’s calendar / 404s or rejections” claim.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager.ts:352 - destination whose credential cannot be resolved is silently skipped with no log and no error result, so the booking reports success while that host's calendar event is never created

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleNewBooking.ts:1073 - evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars) silently no-ops when the array is null, dropping every team member's destination calendar without error for collective events where the organizer has no destination calendar

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager.ts:552 - merge path still uses find (first match only) to delete only the first calendar reference while createAllCalendarEvents now produces one reference per host destination, orphaning stale events on other hosts' calendars after reschedule-with-merge

adjudication_records.issue_text: create.handler.ts:151 - slug spread condition inverted from the original: sets slug when team billing is enabled instead of disabled, so organizations are created with no slug when team billing is disabled, potentially throwing a 500 on a previously-working operation

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleNewBooking.ts:727 - client-input failure (empty/invalid dynamicUserList) is reported as a 500 instead of a 400 because the new plain Error bypasses the HttpError/Prisma branch; also raw Prisma error messages are forwarded to the client in the 400 branch

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts, the new loadUsers() wrapper throws a plain `Error` when `dynamicUserList` is missing/empty (`throw new Error("dynamicUserList is not properly defined or empty.")`). The catch block only maps `HttpError` or `Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError` to a 400; all other errors become `new HttpError({ statusCode: 500, message: "Unable to load users" })`, so this client-input validation failure is incorrectly surfaced as 500.
